submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on a restrictive relative pronoun (' that', less on ' which'/' who', with no comma before it) that opens a relative clause on an indefinite noun phrase naming something wanted, needed, sought or being made (object of want/need/look for/create/build/develop/make/craft, e.g. 'I want a car[[ that]]', 'to develop analgesics[[ that]]'), i.e. a clause about the required properties of a not-yet-existing or hypothetical thing. It is weak (under ~0.2 of max) when the head noun is an existing referent (saw/have/used/found/heard a ...), definite ('the car that' about half), the sentence subject ('The man that came'), or the clause is non-restrictive (', which'), and silent for complementizer or conjunction 'that' ('hope that', 'so that', 'the fact that') and for demonstrative 'That'.
